name.text: A plan that meets a profit target

questiontext.text:
{@E[1]@}

Give a whole-number plan that satisfies both conditions and makes a profit of at least Ksh \({@thou(TT)@}\). There is more than one right answer.

\(x =\) [[input:ans1]] [[validation:ans1]] \(y =\) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]]

[[feedback:prt1]]

generalfeedback.text:
The conditions are \({@a1@}x + {@b1@}y \le {@c1@}\) and \({@a2@}x + {@b2@}y \le {@c2@}\), with \(x \ge 0\), \(y \ge 0\). The profit is \(P = {@pp@}x + {@pq@}y\). Plans near the corner where the two boundary lines meet give the most profit.

For example \(x = {@g1[1]@}\), \(y = {@g1[2]@}\) needs \({@a1*g1[1]+b1*g1[2]@}\) {@un[1]@} and \({@a2*g1[1]+b2*g1[2]@}\) {@un[2]@}, and makes Ksh \({@thou(pp*g1[1]+pq*g1[2])@}\). There are \({@ng@}\) plans that work.

questiondescription.text:
Linear Programming: a plan that meets a profit target

Grade 12 CBE Core 1.4 (d) / Essential 1.4 (d): Construct a whole-number plan that satisfies two resource constraints and reaches a given profit.

Core and Essential

This question is original to this project.

node.sans: is(a1*ans1 + b1*ans2 <= c1 and ans1 >= 0 and ans2 >= 0)

falsefeedback.text:
[[if test='is(ans1 < 0 or ans2 < 0)']]

The numbers made cannot be negative.

[[else]]

Your plan needs \({@a1@} \times {@ans1@} + {@b1@} \times {@ans2@} = {@a1*ans1+b1*ans2@}\) {@un[1]@}, but there are only \({@c1@}\).

[[/if]]
Your plan needs \({@a2@} \times {@ans1@} + {@b2@} \times {@ans2@} = {@a2*ans1+b2*ans2@}\) {@un[2]@}, but there are only \({@c2@}\).
Your plan is possible but makes Ksh \({@thou(pp*ans1+pq*ans2)@}\), which is less than Ksh \({@thou(TT)@}\). Make more of the item with the bigger profit while the conditions allow.
